summary: The animate skill's recipes file gives ready-to-build CSS and JS for the animations that come up most: button press, dropdown/popover/menu/select, tooltip, modal, drawer, toast, accordion, staggered group entrance, hold-to-confirm, tab indicator, scroll reveal, drag-to-dismiss, a blur-masked crossfade and programmatic WAAPI motion. Each recipe fixes exact durations, curves (the --ease-out, --ease-in-out and --ease-drawer tokens), starting scales, transform origins and the detail most implementations miss, such as neighbouring tooltips opening instantly, dismissing a drag on velocity as well as distance, or clipping a duplicated tab list instead of timing colour changes. It also says where each recipe belongs (scroll reveal on marketing only, stagger only for lists seen occasionally, hold-to-confirm for destructive actions). For a design system, it is a per-component motion specification that can become component motion tokens and default behaviours [inferred].
key_ideas: Start from a recipe and adapt it rather than building motion from scratch.
A press scales the whole button to 0.97, labels and icons included, so it reads as a physical press.
Popovers, dropdowns and tooltips scale out of their trigger using the supplied transform origin; the modal is the one popover that stays centered.
Tooltips are faster than popovers, and once one is open its neighbours open with no delay and no animation.
A modal's backdrop fades together with the modal so they read as one surface.
Drawers slide up from translateY(100%) over 500ms on the --ease-drawer curve, the way Vaul hides a drawer; add drag and it becomes a gesture problem.
Toast motion is tuned to the component's personality: plain ease and slightly slower than typical UI.
Accordion height animation costs layout on every frame, so it stays short and animates to a measured height, not auto.
Stagger is decorative, reserved for occasionally seen groups, and must never block interaction.
Hold-to-confirm uses a clip-path fill that is slow and linear on press (it is a progress indicator) and snappy on release.
Clipping a styled duplicate of the tab list keeps text and background colour changes perfectly in sync.
Scroll reveals are for marketing surfaces only and fire once.
Drag-to-dismiss uses springs, dismisses on a fast flick as well as on distance, and needs pointer capture, multi-touch protection, damping and friction past edges.
When a crossfade still shows two objects swapping, a small blur blends them into one perceived change.
WAAPI gives CSS-grade, interruptible, hardware-accelerated motion from JS with no bundle cost.

rules.rule: Start from the matching recipe and adapt it; do not rebuild common animations from scratch.
rules.why: The recipes are ready-to-build implementations for the cases that come up most.

rules.rule: Write the recipes' curves as the --ease-out, --ease-in-out and --ease-drawer tokens defined in SKILL.md, referenced with var().
rules.why: The source states that the recipes' curves are the tokens defined in SKILL.md.
rules.evidence: Curves are the --ease-out, --ease-in-out, and --ease-drawer tokens defined in SKILL.md

rules.rule: Give every pressable element press feedback: transition: transform 160ms var(--ease-out) and transform: scale(0.97) on :active.
rules.why: Instant feedback that the interface heard the user.

rules.rule: Apply the press scale to the whole button so the label and icons scale with it.
rules.why: scale() scales children too, which is what makes it read as a physical press.

rules.rule: Leave the :active press ungated, and gate any :hover styling separately.
rules.why: :active is a real press on touch, so it needs no hover gating.
rules.evidence: No hover gating needed here: :active is a real press on touch. Gate any :hover styling separately.

rules.rule: Scale dropdowns, popovers, menus, selects and tooltips out of their trigger with transform-origin: var(--transform-origin).
rules.why: The transform-origin is the whole point: the panel should look like it came out of the thing you clicked.
rules.evidence: Dropdown, popover, menu, select: The transform-origin is the whole point; Tooltip uses the same origin

rules.rule: Transition dropdown, popover, menu and select opacity and transform over 200ms var(--ease-out), entering from and exiting to opacity: 0 and transform: scale(0.95) ([data-starting-style] and [data-ending-style]).
rules.why: The recipe for panels that scale out of their trigger, not out of thin air.

rules.rule: Transition tooltip transform and opacity over 125ms var(--ease-out), entering from and exiting to opacity: 0 and transform: scale(0.97).
rules.why: Same shape as a popover, faster.

rules.rule: Keep an initial delay before the first tooltip opens.
rules.why: The initial delay prevents accidental activation.
rules.evidence: The initial delay prevents accidental activation

rules.rule: Once one tooltip is open, open neighbouring tooltips instantly by skipping both the delay and the animation (transition-duration: 0ms on [data-instant]).
rules.why: The initial delay prevents accidental activation; after that, skipping both the delay and the animation makes the whole toolbar feel faster.
rules.evidence: Tooltip: the detail most implementations miss; Once one tooltip is open, neighbours open instantly

rules.rule: Keep modals centered with transform-origin: center; they are exempt from the trigger origin.
rules.why: The modal is the one popover that stays centered: it is not anchored to a trigger.
rules.evidence: Modal: The one popover that stays centered; exempt — not anchored to a trigger

rules.rule: Transition modal opacity and transform over 250ms var(--ease-out), entering from and exiting to opacity: 0 and transform: scale(0.96).
rules.why: The source's modal recipe values; it gives no separate reason for 250ms or 0.96.

rules.rule: Fade the modal backdrop's opacity alongside the modal with the same timing (opacity 250ms var(--ease-out)).
rules.why: So the modal and backdrop read as one surface.
rules.evidence: Animate the backdrop's opacity alongside it

rules.rule: Animate drawers and sheets with transform: translateY(0) when open and translateY(100%) when closed ([data-closed]), over 500ms var(--ease-drawer).
rules.why: This is how Vaul hides a drawer before animating it in.

rules.rule: When a drawer can be dragged, treat it as a gesture and follow the drag-to-dismiss recipe.
rules.why: Add drag and it becomes a gesture problem.
rules.evidence: Add drag and it becomes a gesture problem

rules.rule: Animate toasts in from opacity: 0 and translateY(100%) using @starting-style, transitioning opacity and transform over 400ms ease.
rules.why: The source's toast recipe; its plain ease and slower timing are tuned to the toast's personality rather than to the generic UI budget.

rules.rule: Use ease rather than ease-out for toasts and run them slightly slower than typical UI, tuning motion to the component's personality.
rules.why: Sonner reads as elegant partly because its motion is tuned to the component's personality rather than to the generic UI budget.
rules.evidence: ease rather than ease-out, slightly slower than typical UI

rules.rule: Where @starting-style is not available, fall back to a mount flag (useEffect(() => { setMounted(true); }, []) with data-mounted={mounted}).
rules.why: Fallback for the toast entry state.
rules.evidence: If @starting-style isn't available, fall back to the mount flag

rules.rule: When stacked toasts reflow, adjust the opacity change against the height change by feel, then check it again the next day.
rules.why: There's no formula for that pair.
rules.evidence: When toasts stack and the list reflows

rules.rule: Animate accordions with overflow: hidden and height and opacity over 200ms var(--ease-out).
rules.why: The source's accordion recipe; it stays short because height costs layout on every frame.

rules.rule: Keep accordion animations short.
rules.why: It is one of the few animations that costs layout on every frame, so a long duration is expensive as well as sluggish.

rules.rule: Do not animate height to auto; measure the content height in JS, or use a headless primitive that supplies it.
rules.why: Stated in the accordion recipe; the source gives no further reason.
rules.evidence: Measure the content height in JS (or use a headless primitive that supplies it) rather than animating to auto

rules.rule: Stagger a group entrance: each item starts at opacity: 0 and transform: translateY(8px) and runs animation: fadeIn 300ms var(--ease-out) forwards to opacity: 1 and translateY(0), with animation-delay 50ms, 100ms and 150ms on the 2nd, 3rd and 4th items.
rules.why: The source's recipe for a list or grid the user sees occasionally.

rules.rule: Do not stagger a list the user scrolls past all day; keep stagger for lists or grids seen occasionally.
rules.why: Stated as the recipe's scope; the source gives no further reason here (SKILL.md's frequency gate gives little or no motion to frequently seen UI) [inferred].
rules.evidence: For a list or grid the user sees occasionally — not for a list they scroll past all day

rules.rule: Never let a stagger block interaction while it plays.
rules.why: Stagger is decorative.
rules.evidence: Stagger is decorative — it must never block interaction

rules.rule: Use hold-to-confirm for destructive actions where a plain click is too easy to fire by accident.
rules.why: A plain click is too easy to fire by accident on a destructive action.
rules.evidence: Hold to confirm: For destructive actions

rules.rule: Build hold-to-confirm with an overlay clipped by clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0) that fills to inset(0 0 0 0) over 2s linear while the button is :active, snaps back over 200ms var(--ease-out) on release, and scale(0.97) on the button while pressed.
rules.why: Press slow and deliberate; release snappy.

rules.rule: Use linear easing for progress fills.
rules.why: The fill is a progress indicator, and progress shouldn't ease.

rules.rule: For a tab indicator with a colour change, do not time individual colour transitions; duplicate the tab list, style the copy as the active state (different background and text colour), clip the copy so only the active tab shows, and animate the clip.
rules.why: Timing individual colour transitions never quite lands; one element being revealed keeps text and background in perfect sync.
rules.evidence: Tab indicator with a color transition

rules.rule: Animate the active tab copy's clip-path (driven by the active tab's position) over 250ms var(--ease-in-out).
rules.why: Tab indicator recipe.

rules.rule: Use scroll reveals only on marketing surfaces, never on functional UI a user visits daily.
rules.why: Scroll reveal recipe scope.

rules.rule: Build scroll reveals by transitioning clip-path from inset(0 0 100% 0) to inset(0 0 0 0) over 600ms var(--ease-in-out) when [data-visible] is set.
rules.why: The source's scroll reveal recipe.

rules.rule: Trigger scroll reveals with IntersectionObserver or Motion's useInView with { once: true, margin: "-100px" }, and fire them only once.
rules.why: Re-animating on every scroll-by is an interface fighting its reader.
rules.evidence: Trigger with IntersectionObserver ... Fire it once

rules.rule: Use springs, not durations, for drag-to-dismiss.
rules.why: The user can reverse mid-motion.
rules.evidence: Drag to dismiss: Springs, not durations

rules.rule: Dismiss a dragged element on a flick as well as on distance: compute velocity = Math.abs(swipeAmount) / timeTaken and dismiss when Math.abs(swipeAmount) >= SWIPE_THRESHOLD or velocity > 0.11.
rules.why: Dismiss on a flick, not just on distance.
rules.evidence: Dismiss on a flick, not just on distance

rules.rule: Set the dragged element's transform directly (element.style.transform = `translateY(${distance}px)`) rather than through a CSS variable on the parent.
rules.why: Driving it through a CSS variable on the parent recalcs styles for every child.
rules.evidence: Set transform on the dragged element directly

rules.rule: Capture the pointer once a drag starts.
rules.why: So the drag continues when the pointer leaves the element's bounds.

rules.rule: Ignore new touch points while a drag is in progress (if (isDragging) return).
rules.why: Otherwise switching fingers mid-drag makes the element jump.

rules.rule: Damp dragging past a natural boundary so the element moves less the further it goes.
rules.why: Real things slow before they stop.

rules.rule: Allow over-drag with rising resistance instead of stopping it at a hard wall.
rules.why: Listed among the four details that separate a good drag from a bad one: friction, not a wall.

rules.rule: Settle a released or interrupted drag with a spring, { type: "spring", duration: 0.5, bounce: 0.2 }, not a duration.
rules.why: So an interrupted drag keeps its velocity.

rules.rule: When two states visibly overlap during a crossfade and no easing or duration tuning fixes it, blur the seam: transition filter and opacity over 200ms ease, with filter: blur(2px) and opacity: 0.7 while transitioning.
rules.why: Without blur the eye reads two distinct objects swapping; blur blends them into one perceived transformation.
rules.evidence: Masking a crossfade that won't settle

rules.rule: Keep blur under 20px.
rules.why: Heavy blur is expensive, especially in Safari.

rules.rule: When motion needs JS control but not a dependency, use WAAPI (element.animate()), for example a clip-path reveal with { duration: 1000, fill: 'forwards', easing: 'cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1)' }.
rules.why: WAAPI gives CSS-grade performance: hardware-accelerated, interruptible, no bundle cost.

decisions.question: Should list or grid items enter together or one after another?

options.name: Staggered entrance
options.effect: Items fade up from translateY(8px) one after another, 50ms apart, each over 300ms.
options.when: A list or grid the user sees occasionally.

options.name: All at once / no entrance
options.effect: Items appear together without a sequence.
options.when: Lists the user scrolls past all day.

decisions.recommendation: Stagger only occasionally seen groups, and never let it block interaction.

decisions.question: How should toasts move: to the generic UI budget or tuned to the component's personality?

options.name: Generic UI budget
options.effect: ease-out and a typical short UI duration.

options.name: Tuned to personality
options.effect: Plain ease and slightly slower (400ms), which reads as elegant.

decisions.recommendation: Tune toast motion to its personality: 400ms ease from translateY(100%).

decisions.question: How should a destructive action be confirmed?

options.name: Plain click
options.effect: Fires immediately; easy to trigger by accident.

options.name: Hold to confirm
options.effect: A fill sweeps across the button over 2s while held and snaps back in 200ms on release.
options.when: Destructive actions where a plain click is too easy to fire by accident.

decisions.recommendation: Hold to confirm for destructive actions that are too easy to fire by accident.

decisions.question: How should a tab indicator change colour when the active tab changes?

options.name: Individual colour transitions
options.effect: Text and background colours interpolate separately, and the timing never quite lands.

options.name: Clipped duplicate tab list
options.effect: A styled copy of the tabs is revealed by an animated clip, so text and background change in perfect sync.
options.when: Tab lists with a colour change on the active tab.

decisions.recommendation: Clip a duplicated, active-styled tab list and animate the clip over 250ms var(--ease-in-out).
decisions.evidence: Tab indicator with a color transition

decisions.question: When should a drag dismiss the element?

options.name: Distance only
options.effect: Dismisses only past a set swipe threshold; a fast short flick does not dismiss [inferred].

options.name: Distance or velocity
options.effect: Dismisses past the threshold or on a fast flick (velocity > 0.11).
options.when: Drag-to-dismiss surfaces, such as a draggable drawer.

decisions.recommendation: Dismiss on distance or velocity, and settle with a spring so interrupted drags keep their velocity.

decisions.question: How should an element's entry state be set up?

options.name: CSS @starting-style
options.effect: The browser animates from the starting style on mount with no JS.

options.name: Mount flag
options.effect: A useEffect sets mounted to true and a data-mounted attribute drives the transition.

decisions.recommendation: Use @starting-style and fall back to the mount flag.

decisions.question: What to do when a crossfade still shows two overlapping states?

options.name: Keep tuning easing and duration
options.effect: Often still reads as two objects swapping.

options.name: Blur the seam
options.effect: blur(2px) and opacity 0.7 during the transition blend the states into one perceived change.
options.when: When no amount of easing or duration tuning fixes it.

decisions.recommendation: Add a small blur (under 20px) once tuning fails.
decisions.evidence: Masking a crossfade that won't settle

process.detail: Find the recipe for the component (button press, dropdown, tooltip, modal, drawer, toast, accordion, stagger, hold-to-confirm, tab indicator, scroll reveal, drag-to-dismiss) and start from it, then adapt.

process.step: Build a tab indicator by clipping
process.detail: Duplicate the tab list, style the copy as active (background and text colour), clip it so only the active tab shows, and animate the clip-path from the active tab's position over 250ms var(--ease-in-out).

Set transform directly on the element while dragging, capture the pointer, ignore extra touch points, damp and add friction past edges, dismiss on distance or velocity > 0.11, and settle with a spring (duration 0.5, bounce 0.2).

process.step: Tune stacked toast reflow by feel
process.detail: Adjust the opacity change against the height change until it feels right, then check it again the next day.
If easing and duration tuning fail, add filter: blur(2px) and opacity 0.7 during the transition, both over 200ms ease, keeping blur under 20px.

caveats: Recipes are web-only CSS and JS; the data-starting-style, data-ending-style and data-instant attributes assume a component library that sets them (Base UI is named only for --transform-origin) [inferred].
The tab indicator's clip-path: inset(0 60% 0 20%) is a placeholder; the source says the real values are driven by the active tab's position.
SWIPE_THRESHOLD is referenced but its value is not given.

Several recipes exceed the skill's 'UI animations stay under 300ms' rule (toast 400ms, drawer 500ms, scroll reveal 600ms, WAAPI example 1000ms); the source justifies the toast by personality and scroll reveal by being marketing-only [inferred for the comparison].
The stagger recipe uses keyframes, while the skill forbids keyframes only for rapidly triggered elements; stagger is scoped to occasionally seen groups [inferred].
Values are pinned to commit 85e8e23 of emilkowalski/skills (MIT).
The tooltip's initial delay is mentioned but its length is not given.

The source says 'Start from the recipe, then adapt', so exact recipe durations, scales and offsets are marked should; must is kept for what the source states as a rule (trigger transform origin, centered modal, instant neighbouring tooltips, short accordions, stagger never blocking and not on all-day lists, linear progress, clipped tab list, marketing-only scroll reveal fired once, springs and the four drag details, blur under 20px) [inferred].
